author: reek
body: The pump is a three-phase machine driven from the consumer's own poll loop, one action per call: idle arms a single interrupt IN transfer; armed checks the event ring without blocking; drain walks the decoder one event per call until the previous report has converged on the current one, then returns to idle. No transfer is armed while draining, so the report buffer is stable under the decoder's feet. A key struck and released entirely between two reports is dropped -- exactly the mailbox discipline GopKey defends: input that arrived while the machine was busy must not replay into whatever screen appears next.

author: reek
body: Two counters in the state block, which is 64 zeroed bytes with only the phase at offset 0. They exist because "the keyboard enumerated" and "the keyboard delivers" are different claims and this driver could report only the first.

author: reek
body: A single Y/n line collapses the middle two into "Y" and reads exactly like the last one, which is how a keyboard that enumerates perfectly and delivers nothing looks healthy to its own diagnostic.

author: reek
body: `ar` is how many TRBs this driver has pushed. It is the discriminator the pair above cannot give: **if `ev` climbs while `ar` stands still, the controller is completing transfers we never armed** -- a stale ring position or a cycle-bit fault -- and every "completion" counted so far was a re-read of a TRB already consumed, which would produce exactly the empty buffer on the glass. If they climb together, each arm completes once and the ring is walking correctly.

author: reek
body: A STICKY count of reports that carried any non-zero byte, because the hex dump it replaces was a snapshot once per second and a keypress can fall between two repaints. This one cannot be missed: if the device has ever delivered a byte since boot, it is non-zero, and if it reads 0 after a key has been held then every report this driver has ever been handed was eight zeroes.

author: reek
body: Walk the root ports for the first device carrying a boot keyboard interface -- the mass-storage stick on port one is somebody else's device.

author: reek
body: Drain hands the mailbox one scancode per call, the same overwrite the PS/2 interrupt handler performs. The store is the low dword only: the cell's high half is zero from boot and every ISR store is zero-extended, and gk-take masks to the low byte besides. When the decoder reports no remaining difference, the previous report has converged and the next call re-arms.

author: reek
body: The pump above stops at the handback: the controller is no longer ours, and ringing a doorbell on a device firmware has re-owned is how a working machine is turned into a hung one. The guard is a single cell read on the idle path, which is what this loop can afford.

author: reek
body: The consumer-facing read: pump once, then consume the mailbox. With no USB keyboard connected the pump is a single flag test and this is gk-take exactly; with one connected, USB scancodes land in the same cell the PS/2 interrupt handler fills, so a consumer polling this sees whichever keyboard the machine actually has.
